index.title: croc field notes: secure file transfer explained
index.description: Notes and release updates from inside croc: live relays, PAKE encryption, browser transfers, temporary storage, and what changed in each version.
index.imageAlt: An open field notebook containing simple symbols for a relay, code tiles, a key, and a file.

posts.title: From croc v10 to v11
posts.seoTitle: croc v11: Features and Fixes from v11.0.0 to v11.1.1
posts.description: croc v11 makes the handshake harder to confuse, lets one encrypted stored transfer serve a group, starts the web client faster, and closes several unsafe edge cases.
posts.imageAlt: Three black-and-white panels use a shield, group, and lightning icon to represent the croc v11 release.

posts.title: Why croc works this way
posts.description: croc started with a large documentary, a friend in another country, and the surprisingly difficult question of how to send her the file.
posts.imageAlt: Two computers connected by a direct line, with a shared key and confirmation checkmark.

posts.title: The relay is not a waiting room
posts.description: The croc relay looks a little like an upload server, except it does not wait for the whole file before sending it onward.
posts.imageAlt: Two devices connected through a central relay, with three file packets moving between them.

posts.title: What the three words are doing
posts.description: I wanted a croc code to be easy to read aloud. Making three ordinary words secure enough for a file transfer takes a little more work.
posts.imageAlt: Blank code tiles converge into one cryptographic key.

posts.title: PAKE, step by step
posts.description: PAKE is the part of croc that turns a small shared phrase into a strong key. Here is the exchange without skipping the interesting bits.
posts.imageAlt: Two computers exchange messages and independently derive the same cryptographic key.

posts.title: Send a file without installing anything
posts.description: The browser can join an ordinary croc transfer now. Choose the files, share the code, and keep the tab open until the handoff finishes.
posts.imageAlt: A web browser sends a file directly to a receiving device.

posts.title: A browser and a terminal can share the same file
posts.description: The browser client was meant to join normal croc transfers, not become another file-sharing island with its own links and accounts.
posts.imageAlt: A browser window and command-line terminal are connected by a file transfer.

posts.title: When both computers cannot be online at once
posts.description: Direct croc transfers expect both computers to be awake. Stored mode is for the inconvenient times when the people are not.
posts.imageAlt: A locked parcel waits for a limited time and a configured number of verified downloads.

posts.title: Send one file to a group, on their schedule
posts.description: Stored mode can give several people time to retrieve the same encrypted file. Choose a download allowance, choose a deadline, and share one link.
posts.imageAlt: One locked parcel branches toward three recipient devices while a clock marks the shared download window.

posts.title: 36 ways to send a file
posts.seoTitle: 36 Ways to Send a File: croc and 35 Alternatives
posts.description: Compare croc with 35 file transfer tools by resume support, account requirements, browser and CLI transfers, encryption, availability, and transfer paths.
posts.imageAlt: File transfer tools comparison showing one file connected to browser, CLI, desktop, mobile, cloud, and synchronization routes.
